content: 1. Exercise caution and monitor when co-administering drugs metabolized predominantly by CYP3A, as dose adjustments may be necessary. Crizotinib increases erythromycin stearate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. 2. ECG monitoring is recommended when using drugs that may prolong the QT interval. Crofelemer increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Crofelemer may also inhibit MRP2 and OATP1A2 transporters in the gut but is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. 3. Erythromycin stearate increases cyclosporine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, and cyclosporine increases erythromycin stearate levels through other mechanisms. Monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin stearate increases dabigatran levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 5. Dabrafenib decreases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 6. Erythromycin stearate increases dactinomycin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 7. Danicopan increases erythromycin stearate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where small concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases dapsone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Erythromycin stearate increases daridorexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit daridorexant dose to 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Erythromycin stearate increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 11. Both dasatinib and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases daunorubicin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 13. Deferasirox decreases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases deflazacort levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 15. Both deutetrabenazine and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QT interval, especially under conditions that increase torsades de pointes risk. 16. Erythromycin stearate increases dexamethasone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 17. Erythromycin stearate increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. 18. Erythromycin stearate decreases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor for adverse effects like nausea, irregular bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases digoxin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 20. Erythromycin stearate increases disopyramide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Erythromycin stearate increases docetaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 22. Both dolasetron and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin stearate increases donepezil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Erythromycin stearate increases doxorubicin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 25. Erythromycin stearate increases dutasteride levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Duvelisib increases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Elagolix increases erythromycin stearate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates and adjust doses as needed. 29. Eliglustat decreases erythromycin stearate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 30. Eluxadoline increases erythromycin stearate levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious events. 32. Encorafenib affects erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4. Monitor for increased exposure and adjust doses of OATP1B3 substrates as needed. 33. Erythromycin stearate increases eplerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Erythromycin stearate increases erlotinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 35. Erythromycin stearate decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases etoposide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases eucalyptus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Erythromycin stearate increases exemestane levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Both ezogabine and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QT interval when co-administered. 40. Fedratinib increases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust doses of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 41. Erythromycin stearate increases finasteride levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Erythromycin stearate increases finerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium and adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 43. Both flecainide and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 44. Erythromycin stearate increases fludrocortisone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 45. Both fluoxetine and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases fluvastatin toxicity via OATP1B1 inhibition, increasing the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 47. Both fluvoxamine and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 48. Both foscarnet and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 49. Fostamatinib increases erythromycin stearate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrate drugs and adjust dosages as needed. 50. Fostemsavir increases erythromycin stearate levels via OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QT interval and adjust therapy as needed. 51. Both gadobenate and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 52. Both gemtuzumab and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 53. Erythromycin stearate increases gentamicin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 54. Erythromycin stearate increases gepirone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 55. Goserelin increases erythromycin stearate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor. 56. Erythromycin stearate increases guanfacine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. Adjust therapy and monitor closely.
